## Overview:

This PR changes `loadUser` to return `userId` instead of `id`, while leaving the exported `User` type and `Promise<User>` return contract unchanged. This appears intended to refine the user identifier naming, but the implementation and declared contract are now inconsistent.

The main risk is a TypeScript type-checking failure and/or runtime API break for callers expecting `User.id`. Specialist review should verify intended identifier naming and affected consumers.

## Strengths:

- Minimal, focused one-line implementation change.
- Preserves existing database lookup, display-name mapping, and not-found behavior.

resolvedReview.overview:
This one-line PR changes `loadUser` in `src/users.ts` to return `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }` instead of `{ id: row.id, name: row.display_name }`. The PR description says it refines behavior "while preserving existing contracts," but the exported type contract is left untouched.

That creates a direct contradiction: `export type User = { id: string; name: string };` and the declared return type `Promise<User>` still require `id`, while the returned object literal now provides `userId` and omits `id`. The lookup, not-found error path, and display-name mapping are otherwise unchanged.

findings.title: [P0] Return the declared `id` field instead of `userId`
findings.body: The changed line returns an object that cannot satisfy the declared return type. `User` requires `id: string` and has no `userId` property, so under standard TypeScript type-checking this file fails to compile regardless of configuration: missing required property `id` (TS2741) and excess property `userId` on the literal (TS2353) — missing-property errors are unconditional, not strictness-dependent. Even if type errors were bypassed by a transpile-only pipeline, every successful `loadUser` call would return a shape violating its exported contract, leaving `user.id` `undefined` for all consumers. This also contradicts the PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts." Fix by restoring `id: row.id`, or — if the rename is intentional — updating `export type User` (and any consumers) in the same change.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This one-line PR changes `loadUser` in `src/users.ts` to return `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }` instead of `{ id: row.id, name: row.display_name }`. The PR description says it refines behavior "while preserving existing contracts," but the exported type contract is left untouched.

That creates a direct contradiction: `export type User = { id: string; name: string };` and the declared return type `Promise<User>` still require `id`, while the returned object literal now provides `userId` and omits `id`. The lookup, not-found error path, and display-name mapping are otherwise unchanged.

## Verification

Verification was not run: `pr_review_verify` discovery reported verification is disabled because no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured, so no baseline name was applicable. Note that baseline execution runs PR code unsandboxed (network/filesystem access is not restricted; lifecycle supervision only signals the original POSIX process group), which is one reason it requires an explicit user-level opt-in. Findings below were instead validated by direct source reads of `src/users.ts` (the repository contains exactly this one file; no other callers or tests exist).

## Findings

### [P0] Return the declared `id` field instead of `userId`
**Severity:** P0
**Rationale:** The changed line returns an object that cannot satisfy the declared return type. `User` requires `id: string` and has no `userId` property, so under standard TypeScript type-checking this file fails to compile regardless of configuration: missing required property `id` (TS2741) and excess property `userId` on the literal (TS2353) — missing-property errors are unconditional, not strictness-dependent. Even if type errors were bypassed by a transpile-only pipeline, every successful `loadUser` call would return a shape violating its exported contract, leaving `user.id` `undefined` for all consumers. This also contradicts the PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts." Fix by restoring `id: row.id`, or — if the rename is intentional — updating `export type User` (and any consumers) in the same change.
**Location:** `src/users.ts:11 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

Five of six requested lanes completed: `overview`, `conventions-maintainability`, `correctness`, `correctness-contracts`, and `security-performance`. The `performance-resources` lane returned `partial` twice (initial batch and a same-policy rerun) with retained raw evidence "NO FINDINGS"; it was covered inline — a single object-key rename adds no allocations, I/O, unbounded work, or ownership/cleanup change, so no performance/resource finding exists.

## Strengths and notes

- Minimal, focused diff with clean separation of the lookup, error, and mapping concerns already in place; the not-found guard and `display_name` mapping are preserved.
- Correctness (state/concurrency), security, and performance lanes found no additional issues in the changed lines.

All requested lanes completed or were covered inline; one P0 blocking finding remains.
